title: Oppo Find N6 5G 512GB (Stellar Titanium) $2,799 + Delivery ($0 C&C/ in-Store) @ JB Hi-Fi
body:

[DealMunger] Yeah but see and feel the quality mate.. Oppo is a way quality brand.. I have owned iPhone and Oppo I will still go for Oppo battery lasts longer and don't slows down on every update like Apple..
[FlyingMiffy] @iSmart: The fact you called yourself iSmart means you're an Apple fanboi. That means no matter the quality of the product, you're never going to like it. The OPPO N6 is well reviewed and its known as THE best folding device out there. This price is about 20% off regular.
[Mi2] I got a Vivo which is very similar to Oppo as both are owned by BBK and it's far better than crappy Samsung flagships that I had.
No over heating, no battery drain and I don't care about extra features that Samsung offers.
Hard to find any Samsung phone with 1TB of storage at $1400 and it has everything I need.
Still I don't pay this amount of money for a phone regardless of the brand.

[DealMunger] Go to a nice JB hifi store where people don't vandalise and scratch/dig the screens for fun.. I don't to my personal phone, do you?
[yak] A $2.8k phone should be tougher. If you expect a phone to cost you $365 per year (not including telco network connection), then this device should last you nearly 8 years to be worth it.
If it can’t last 8 minutes before screen peeling in JBHiFi then it has no chance lasting 8 years in an Australian’s sweaty pocket.
Unless you have a business usecase for this or you’re a cutting-edge-tech tragic, then this is a bad deal.
[asdaf1118] It isn't any less or more durable than any other fold. People who spend 3k on a phone aren't using it for 8 years, especially a foldable. Noone needs a foldable but this is like saying every foldable on the market is a bad deal lol. Money and use case = no issue.
[BradH13] All the folds are equally fragile.
You don't buy one if you can't just accept it.
It's definitely not a mainstream form factor and likely never will be.

I switched to oppo n6 after reviewd tons of youtube.

Sony Experias are pretty cool like that.
Raw photos, and 4k HDR video directly onto removable storage is great. The option for a wired mic is also handy.
Normally its the price that kills the hype, but since we're comparing to almost $3k, not so much.
Modern storage limits rarely even fit my music library now its all flac. I really need to re-encode a second copy to OPUS for on-the-go use, listening environments are seldom 'FLAC worthy'.
